tip: Κάνω τραπέζι (káno trapézi) = I treat someone to a meal – literally 'I make a table'.
Με τα πόδια (me ta pódhia) = on foot – literally 'with the feet'.
Ξεκουράζομαι (ksekurázome) = I rest – ξε- undoes κουράζομαι (kurázome = I get tired).
Αργεί (arghí) = he is late – Greek has a whole verb for running late, αργώ (arghó).
Λόγω (lógho) = because of; the noun after it changes ending: κίνηση (kínisi) becomes λόγω κίνησης (lógho kínisis = because of traffic).
Κάνω διάλειμμα (káno dhiálima) = I take a break – Greek normally makes a break rather than takes one.
Δουλεύω (dhulévo) = I work, but it covers machines running too: δεν δουλεύει (dhen dhulévi = it's not working).
Κατεβάζω (katevázo) = I download – literally 'I bring down'.
Πάω για μπάνιο (páo ya bánio) = I go for a swim – μπάνιο is both bath and swim.
Τα βράδια (ta vrádhia) = in the evenings – a time word in the plural usually means it happens habitually.
Πάμε βόλτα (páme vólta) = let's go for a stroll – βόλτα stays bare here, with no article.
Οι καθημερινές (i kathimerinés) = weekdays – literally 'the everyday ones'.
Κάνω ησυχία (káno isikhía) = I keep quiet – midday quiet hours are taken seriously in Greece.
Clock times take τις: για τις οχτώ (ya tis okhtó) = for 8 o'clock – without τις it normally means for 8 people.
Κατά τις εννιά (katá tis eniá) = around nine – κατά (katá) turns a clock time into a rough one.
Order έναν διπλό ελληνικό (énan dipló ellinikó = a double Greek coffee) by sweetness: σκέτο (skéto = plain), μέτριο (métrio = medium), γλυκό (ghlikó = sweet).
Μέτριος (métrios) = medium-sweet coffee – the most common way Greeks order it.
Το στέκι (to stéki) is a friend group's fixed hangout – the café or bar where your παρέα (paréa = group of friends) usually ends up.
Η παρέα (i paréa) = your group of friends – a core Greek social institution.
Δεν... ποτέ (dhen... poté) = never – Greek keeps both negative words.
Την άλλη εβδομάδα (tin áli evdhomádha) = next week – literally 'the other week'.
Κλείνω (klíno = close) is the booking verb for appointments too: έκλεισα ραντεβού (éklisa randevú = I booked an appointment).
Πέρασα από (pérasa apó) = I stopped by – περνάω από (pernáo apó) is literally 'I pass from'.
Από φοιτητής (apó fititís) = since I was a student – the noun keeps its plain dictionary form after από here.
Και (ke) can mean too, not just and: αγαπάω και το ρεπό (aghapáo ke to repó = I love my day off too).
The body part is the subject: πονάει ο λαιμός μου (ponái o lemós mu = my throat hurts).
Many body-state verbs end in -ομαι (-ome) and already mean get: ζαλίζομαι (zalízome = I get dizzy), σηκώνομαι (sikónome = I get up).
Βήχω (víkho) = I cough; έβηχε (évikhe) is the ongoing past, for something that kept happening all evening.
Κρυώνω (krióno) = I feel cold, but the past κρύωσα (kríosa) = I caught a cold.
Μετράω τον πυρετό (metráo ton piretó) = literally 'I measure the fever', the way to say take a temperature.
